examples.ko: 갑자기 불이 나가서 퓨즈를 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: The lights suddenly went out, so I checked the fuse.
The fuse blew, so the microwave won't run.
My father replaced the old fuse with a new one.

examples.ko: 자동차 퓨즈 상자는 보통 운전석 쪽 대시보드 아래에 있어요.
examples.en: A car's fuse box is usually under the dashboard on the driver's side.
Do you know how many amps this fuse is rated for?

examples.ko: 전기 제품을 너무 많이 꽂으면 퓨즈가 나갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you plug in too many appliances, the fuse can blow.

explain: '퓨즈가 나가다', '퓨즈가 끊어지다'처럼 말해요. 집 전체의 전기가 나갔을 때는 보통 '두꺼비집'(차단기)부터 확인해요.
explain_en: People say '퓨즈가 나가다' or '퓨즈가 끊어지다' when a fuse blows. When the power goes out in the whole house, Koreans usually check the '두꺼비집' (breaker box) first.

examples.en: The kids leave school at three in the afternoon.
It rained, so I went home from school with my friend.
I stopped by a convenience store on my way home from school.

examples.ko: 동생이 하교하면 같이 저녁을 먹을 거예요.
examples.en: When my younger sibling gets home from school, we'll have dinner together.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 학생들이 평소보다 일찍 하교해요.
examples.en: During exam week, students leave school earlier than usual.

examples.ko: 하교하고 바로 학원에 가야 해서 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have to go straight to a cram school after school, so it's tiring.

explain: 반대말은 '등교하다'예요. '하교 시간', '하굣길'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. 학생에게만 쓰고, 회사에서 집으로 갈 때는 '퇴근하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '등교하다'. It also appears in nouns such as '하교 시간' and '하굣길'. It is only for students; leaving work is '퇴근하다'.

examples.ko: 선수들은 대회 전에 한 달 동안 합숙을 해요.
examples.en: The athletes live together for a month before the competition.

examples.ko: 합숙 훈련이 힘들었지만 친구가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The group training camp was hard, but I made many friends.
Our club has a group stay every vacation.

examples.ko: 합숙 비용은 한 사람당 오만 원이에요.
examples.en: The cost of the group stay is fifty thousand won per person.

examples.ko: 합숙 중에는 휴대폰을 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't use your phone during the group stay.
Most trainees live together in a dormitory.

explain: '합숙 훈련', '합숙소', '합숙 생활'로 자주 써요. 운동팀이나 연습생처럼 정해진 목표가 있는 그룹에 쓰고, 친구들끼리 놀러 가서 자는 건 합숙이라고 하지 않아요. 동아리의 모임 여행은 'MT'라고 해요.
explain_en: Common combinations are '합숙 훈련', '합숙소', and '합숙 생활'. It is for groups with a shared goal, like sports teams or trainees; friends sleeping over on a trip would not call it '합숙'. A club's group trip is called 'MT'.

examples.en: The athletes are staying together ahead of the competition.
We stayed together at school for a week.

examples.ko: 연습생들이 한 건물에서 합숙하는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: Trainees often live together in one building.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 친구들과 합숙하며 공부할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to study with my friends, living together, before the exam.
If you stay in the camp, you have to exercise together every morning.

examples.ko: 팀원 모두 합숙해서 서로 많이 친해졌어요.
examples.en: The whole team lived together, so we got much closer.

explain: 운동팀, 연습생, 수련회처럼 목표가 있는 단체 일정에 써요. 친구 집에서 같이 자는 건 '같이 자다'라고 말해요. 명사 '합숙'은 '합숙 훈련'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it for group schedules with a goal, such as sports teams, trainees, or retreats. Sleeping over at a friend's place is just '같이 자다'. The noun '합숙' appears in '합숙 훈련'.

examples.en: My parents went to Jeju Island to relax.
This town is famous as a resort city.
I needed a rest, so I took a week of vacation.
I relaxed with my family at a seaside resort.

examples.ko: 할머니는 시골에서 조용한 휴양 생활을 하세요.
examples.en: My grandmother lives a quiet, restful life in the countryside.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 따뜻한 나라로 휴양 가는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: In winter, many people go to warm countries for a getaway.

explain: '휴양지', '휴양림', '휴양 시설'처럼 합쳐서 많이 써요. 휴양은 쉬는 것이 목적이라서, 구경이 중심인 '관광'과 달라요. 말할 때는 '휴양하다'보다 '쉬러 가다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is often combined, as in '휴양지', '휴양림', and '휴양 시설'. Resting is the point, unlike '관광', which is about sightseeing. In speech people usually say '쉬러 가다' instead.

examples.ko: 의사가 한 달 동안 시골에서 휴양하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to rest in the countryside for a month.
He read books while relaxing at the beach.
My hobby is getting away to the mountains every weekend.
I rested at home until my body recovered.
The hotel is full of people who came to relax.
This summer I'm going to relax on Jeju Island.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '쉬다', '푹 쉬다'가 훨씬 흔해요. '휴양하다'는 병이나 피로를 회복하려고 쉴 때, 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. '휴양지에서 휴양하다'는 말이 겹치니 '휴양지에서 쉬다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: In daily talk '쉬다' or '푹 쉬다' is much more common. '휴양하다' shows up more in writing and news, for resting to recover from illness or fatigue. '휴양지에서 휴양하다' repeats itself, so '휴양지에서 쉬다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I caught a crayfish in the stream.
Crayfish only live in clean water.

examples.ko: 아이들이 돌 밑에 숨은 가재를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The children found a crayfish hiding under a rock.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 시골 계곡에서 가재 잡는 게 제일 재미있었어요.
examples.en: As a kid, catching crayfish in the country valley was the most fun.

examples.ko: 가재 두 마리가 어항 안에 있어요.
examples.en: There are two crayfish in the fish tank.
This crayfish has really big claws.

explain: 한국에서 가재는 보통 맑은 계곡이나 개울에서 잡는 작은 민물 동물이에요. 바다의 큰 '바닷가재'(랍스터)와 달라서, 요리 재료를 말할 때는 '바닷가재'라고 해야 해요.

phrases.example: 가재는 게 편이라고, 두 사람이 서로 감싸 주네요.
phrases.en: People in similar situations take each other's side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처지나 모양이 비슷한 사람끼리 서로 편들어 준다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that people in similar situations side with each other.
phrases.en_equiv: Birds of a feather flock together

explain_en: In Korea 가재 usually means the small freshwater animal caught in clean streams and valleys. It is different from the big sea '바닷가재' (lobster), so for cooking ingredients you must say '바닷가재'.

examples.en: He serves as both professor and research institute director.

examples.ko: 회사 일과 학원 강사를 겸직하면 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's hard to hold both a company job and a tutoring-academy job.

examples.ko: 이사님이 두 부서의 팀장을 겸직하고 있어요.
examples.en: The director is leading two departments at the same time.

examples.ko: 겸직하는 사람은 시간 관리를 잘해야 해요.
examples.en: People who hold two positions need to manage time well.

examples.ko: 규정 때문에 다른 일을 겸직할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Because of the rules, I can't take on another job.
Since last year, this teacher has also served as vice principal.

explain: 'A와 B를 겸직하다'처럼 두 자리를 함께 맡을 때 써요. 회사 규정이나 공무원 이야기에서 '겸직 금지'라는 말을 자주 봐요. 일상 대화에서는 '투잡을 뛰다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used like 'A와 B를 겸직하다' when someone holds two positions together. You often see '겸직 금지' in company rules and in talk about civil servants. In casual talk people also say '투잡을 뛰다'.

examples.en: The new movie was a huge success.
The first show was a big hit, so everyone was happy.
This school festival was a great success.

examples.ko: 작은 가게로 시작했는데 지금은 대성공 사례가 됐어요.
examples.en: It started as a small shop and has now become a big success story.
They say that song is a huge hit overseas too.

examples.ko: 대성공 소식을 듣고 팀원들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The team members clapped when they heard the news of the big success.

explain: '대성공을 거두다', '대성공이다'처럼 써요. 반대는 '대실패'예요. 그냥 '성공'보다 훨씬 크고 기대 이상일 때 써서, 작은 일에 쓰면 과장처럼 들려요.
explain_en: Common patterns are '대성공을 거두다' and '대성공이다'. The opposite is '대실패'. It is much bigger than plain '성공' and beyond expectations, so using it for small things sounds exaggerated.

examples.en: Our school festival was a huge success.
The new product was a big hit, so the factory got busy.
I think this movie will be a big hit.
For a new shop to be a great success, service is important.
The presentation went great, so the team leader praised us.
Even a hugely successful singer was unknown at first.

explain: 결과를 말할 때 '-했어요'로 자주 써요. 구어체로는 '대박 나다'도 많이 써서 '영화가 대박 났어요'라고 해요. 사람에게는 '크게 성공하다'가 더 부드러워요.
explain_en: It is often used in the past tense, '-했어요', to report a result. In casual speech '대박 나다' is also very common, as in '영화가 대박 났어요'. For a person, '크게 성공하다' sounds softer.

examples.en: The puppy keeps sticking close behind me.

examples.ko: 점수 차가 줄어서 상대 팀이 바짝 따라붙었어요.
examples.en: The score gap shrank, and the other team closed in.
The car behind me was tailgating, and it scared me.
A reporter trailing me like a shadow is making things hard.

examples.ko: 마지막 바퀴에서 선두를 따라붙을 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can they catch up with the leader on the last lap?

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 옆에 딱 따라붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The child is sticking right next to her mom.

explain: '따라가다'가 그냥 뒤를 따르는 것이라면, '따라붙다'는 떨어지지 않고 가까이에서 붙는 느낌이에요. 스포츠에서는 점수나 순위 차를 줄여 쫓아갈 때도 써요. 보통 '바짝 따라붙다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '따라가다' simply means to follow, but '따라붙다' feels like staying close without falling away. In sports it also means closing a gap in score or ranking. People often say '바짝 따라붙다'.

examples.en: That old man lived as a drifter his whole life.

examples.ko: 떠돌이 개가 우리 집 앞에 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A stray dog is sitting in front of our house.
He ended his wandering life and returned to his hometown.
A traveling circus came to the village.
The child gave food to a stray cat.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 떠돌이였던 그는 이제 작은 집이 있어요.
examples.en: He was a drifter as a child, but now he has a small house.

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 '떠돌이 개', '떠돌이 고양이'처럼 주인 없이 돌아다니는 동물에도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 조금 불쌍하게 보는 느낌이라서 직접 부르는 말로는 쓰지 않아요. 요즘 동물에게는 '길고양이', '유기견'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used for people and also for animals roaming without an owner, as in '떠돌이 개' and '떠돌이 고양이'. Used for a person, it carries a slightly pitying tone, so you would not call someone that to their face. For animals today, '길고양이' and '유기견' are more common.

examples.ko: 가게 앞에 마네킹 세 개가 서 있어요.
examples.en: Three mannequins are standing in front of the shop.
Try dressing the mannequin in the new clothes.

examples.ko: 그 모델은 마네킹처럼 키가 크고 말랐어요.
examples.en: That model is tall and thin like a mannequin.

examples.ko: 쇼윈도의 마네킹을 보고 같은 옷을 샀어요.
examples.en: I saw the mannequin in the shop window and bought the same outfit.

examples.ko: 점원이 마네킹이 입은 옷과 같은 옷을 가져왔어요.
examples.en: The clerk brought the same outfit the mannequin was wearing.
We practice first aid on a mannequin.

explain: 옷가게에서 '마네킹이 입은 옷 주세요'라고 말하면 점원이 바로 알아들어요. 응급 처치 연습용 사람 모형도 마네킹이라고 해요. 표정 없이 가만히 서 있는 사람에게 '마네킹 같다'고 놀리기도 해요.
explain_en: In a clothing store, saying '마네킹이 입은 옷 주세요' gets you the outfit on display. First-aid practice dummies are also called 마네킹. People tease someone standing still without expression by saying '마네킹 같다'.

examples.en: That painter lived in the countryside in his later years.
I'm saving money from now so my later years will be comfortable.
My grandfather's final years were not lonely.

examples.ko: 작가의 말년 작품은 아주 조용하고 깊어요.
examples.en: The author's late works are very quiet and deep.
I want to spend my last years happily.
He never stopped writing until the end of his life.

explain: '노년'은 나이 든 시기를 가리키고, '말년'은 삶이나 일의 마지막 시기를 가리켜요. 보통 '말년에'로 쓰고, 어르신 앞에서 '말년'이라고 하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 말년 병장이라서 요즘 일을 거의 안 해요.
phrases.en: a soldier near discharge who takes it easy
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 제대할 병장을 가리키는 군대 말이에요. 느긋하게 지내는 사람을 놀릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Military slang for a sergeant close to discharge; also used to tease someone who takes things easy.

explain_en: '노년' refers to old age, while '말년' points to the last stretch of a life or career. It is usually used as '말년에', and saying '말년' in front of an elderly person can be rude.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에서 주인이 몽둥이를 들고 도둑을 쫓아요.
examples.en: In the old tale, the owner chases the thief with a club.
The child picked up a branch as thick as a club.
You must never hit people with a club.
A thick club is lying by the road.

examples.ko: 개를 쫓으려고 집어 든 몽둥이는 너무 무거웠어요.
examples.en: The club I picked up to drive the dog away was too heavy.
The police stopped the person holding a club.

explain: 몽둥이는 사람이나 동물을 때리는 굵고 긴 막대라서 폭력의 느낌이 강해요. 야구에서 치는 막대는 '방망이'라고 하고, '야구 몽둥이'라고 하면 어색해요. '도깨비 방망이'도 몽둥이처럼 생겼지만 '방망이'라고 불러요.
explain_en: A 몽둥이 is a thick, long stick used for hitting, so it feels violent. The bat in baseball is a '방망이', and '야구 몽둥이' sounds odd. The goblin's magic club is also called '도깨비 방망이'.

examples.en: I scraped the fish scales off with a knife.
The fish's scales sparkle in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 뱀의 몸은 단단한 비늘로 덮여 있어요.
examples.en: A snake's body is covered with tough scales.

examples.ko: 생선을 사 오면 먼저 비늘 손질부터 해요.
examples.en: When I bring fish home, I start by dealing with the scales.
Fish with lots of scales are hard to prepare.

examples.ko: 용 그림에는 번쩍이는 비늘이 아주 많이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: The dragon painting has a great many shiny scales drawn on it.

explain: 물고기나 뱀, 용처럼 몸이 작은 조각으로 덮인 동물에 써요. 새의 '깃털', 동물의 '털'과는 다른 말이에요. 요리 전에는 '비늘을 벗기다', '비늘을 긁다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is for animals like fish, snakes, and dragons whose bodies are covered in small plates. It is different from '깃털' (bird feathers) and '털' (fur). Before cooking, people say '비늘을 벗기다' or '비늘을 긁다'.

examples.en: The child spins round and round on the spot.
A helicopter is circling in the sky.
My head was spinning, so I sat down for a moment.

examples.ko: 길을 몰라서 같은 곳을 빙빙 돌았어요.
examples.en: I didn't know the way, so I went around the same place again and again.

examples.ko: 이야기가 빙빙 돌기만 하고 결론이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The talk just goes around in circles with no conclusion.
Birds are flying in circles above the tree.

explain: '빙빙 돌다'로 가장 많이 써요. 작은말 '뱅뱅'은 작고 가벼운 것에, '빙빙'은 그보다 큰 느낌에 써요. 어지러울 때 '머리가 빙빙 돌다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 말을 빙빙 돌리지 말고 핵심부터 말해 주세요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 말을 바로 하지 않고 돌려서 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: To avoid saying what you mean directly and talk around it.

explain_en: The most common pattern is '빙빙 돌다'. The smaller-sounding '뱅뱅' fits small, light things, while '빙빙' feels bigger. When you're dizzy you can say '머리가 빙빙 돌다'.

examples.en: I washed my hands at the sink.
The water in the sink isn't draining well.
There's no soap at the bathroom sink.

examples.ko: 칫솔은 세면대 옆 컵에 꽂아 두세요.
examples.en: Put the toothbrush in the cup next to the sink.
The hotel sink was so small that it was inconvenient.
I bought baking soda to clean the sink.

explain: 한국 집에서는 '세면대'에서 손을 씻고 세수와 양치를 해요. 샤워는 '샤워기' 아래에서 하고, 부엌에서 설거지하는 곳은 '싱크대'예요. 세면대와 싱크대를 서로 바꿔 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: In a Korean home you wash your hands, face, and brush your teeth at the '세면대'. Showers happen under the '샤워기', and the kitchen place for dishes is the '싱크대'. The two words are not swapped.

examples.en: My deaf friend talks in sign language.

examples.ko: 뉴스 화면 아래쪽에 수어 통역이 나와요.
examples.en: A sign language interpreter appears at the bottom of the news screen.
I started studying sign language.
A sign language club has started at our school.
In sign language, you speak with hand shapes and facial expressions.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 영화를 위해 수어를 몇 달 연습했어요.
examples.en: The actor practiced sign language for months for the movie.

explain: 예전에는 '수화'라고 많이 불렀지만, 지금은 '수어'를 공식으로 써요. 한국수어는 한국어를 손으로 옮긴 것이 아니라 문법이 다른 독립된 언어예요. 쓰는 사람은 '수어 사용자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It used to be called '수화', but '수어' is now the official word. 한국수어 is not Korean moved onto the hands; it is a separate language with its own grammar. A signer is a '수어 사용자'.

examples.en: If you have any questions about the contract, please ask.
If you jot down your questions, it's easier to ask them.

examples.ko: 설명을 듣고도 몇 가지 의문점이 남았어요.
examples.en: A few questions remained even after the explanation.
I tried organizing the doubtful points in this report.
I looked for more material to settle my questions.

examples.ko: 아무도 그 사고의 의문점에 답하지 못했어요.
examples.en: No one could answer the open questions about the accident.

explain: '의문점이 있다·생기다·남다·풀리다'처럼 같이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '궁금한 점'이 훨씬 자연스럽고, '의문점'은 회의·보고서·뉴스처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. '의심'은 믿지 못하는 마음이라 의문점과 달라요.
explain_en: It goes with verbs like '있다', '생기다', '남다', and '풀리다'. In everyday talk '궁금한 점' is much more natural; '의문점' fits meetings, reports, and news. '의심' means not trusting, which is different.

examples.en: I majored in anthropology at university.

examples.ko: 인류학 수업에서 여러 나라의 결혼 문화를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In anthropology class, I learned about marriage customs in various countries.

examples.ko: 인류학자는 현지 사람들과 함께 살면서 연구해요.
examples.en: Anthropologists research by living together with local people.
Anthropology looks hard, but the stories are fun.

examples.ko: 인류학 책을 읽고 다른 문화에 관심이 생겼어요.
examples.en: After reading an anthropology book, I became interested in other cultures.

examples.ko: 형은 인류학 박사 과정을 밟고 있어요.
examples.en: My older brother is in a doctoral program in anthropology.

explain: 학문 이름에 사람과 학과를 붙여서 '인류학자', '인류학과'로 써요. '사회학', '고고학'과 가까운데, 인류학은 사람의 문화와 생활 방식을 직접 가서 보는 연구가 많아요. 발음은 [일류학]이에요.
explain_en: Add a person or department ending to get '인류학자' and '인류학과'. It is close to '사회학' and '고고학', but anthropology often involves going out and observing people's culture and ways of life. It is pronounced [일류학].

examples.ko: 겨울에 쓸 장작을 마당에 쌓아 놨어요.
examples.en: I stacked firewood for winter in the yard.
At the campsite, I lit the firewood.
The sound of burning firewood is soothing.

examples.ko: 아버지는 도끼로 장작 패는 일을 잘하세요.
examples.en: My father is good at splitting firewood with an axe.

examples.ko: 젖은 장작은 불이 잘 안 붙어요.
examples.en: Wet firewood doesn't catch fire well.

examples.ko: 장작 한 단을 사서 난로에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I bought a bundle of firewood and put it in the stove.

explain: '장작을 패다'(도끼로 쪼개다), '장작을 쌓다', '장작불'처럼 써요. 불 피우는 나무인 '땔감' 중에서 잘라서 쪼갠 굵은 나무가 장작이에요. 요즘은 캠핑 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Typical phrases are '장작을 패다' (split with an axe), '장작을 쌓다', and '장작불'. Among '땔감' (fuel for fires), 장작 is the thick wood that has been cut and split. These days it comes up often in camping talk.

examples.en: There are a lot of oak trees in the mountains.
Acorns fall from the oak tree.
Meat grilled over oak charcoal tastes good.
We rested under an old oak tree.

examples.ko: 이 집은 참나무로 만든 가구가 많아요.
examples.en: This house has a lot of furniture made of oak.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 참나무 잎이 갈색으로 변해요.
examples.en: In autumn, oak leaves turn brown.

explain: 참나무는 한 종류가 아니라 상수리나무·떡갈나무·갈참나무처럼 도토리가 열리는 여러 나무를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '참나무 숯'은 고기 구울 때 좋은 숯으로 알려져 있어요. 영어의 oak와 완전히 같지는 않지만 비슷하게 번역해요.
explain_en: 참나무 is not one species but a group name for acorn-bearing trees such as 상수리나무, 떡갈나무, and 갈참나무. '참나무 숯' is known as good charcoal for grilling meat. It is translated as oak, though it is not exactly the same.

examples.ko: 이 회사의 창립자는 삼십 년 전에 작은 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: The founder of this company opened a small shop thirty years ago.

examples.ko: 창립자가 직접 학교의 첫 수업을 했어요.
examples.en: The founder taught the school's first class himself.
There is a library named after the founder.

examples.ko: 창립자 이야기가 회사 소개 책자에 나와요.
examples.en: The founder's story appears in the company brochure.

examples.ko: 그 단체는 창립자가 돌아가신 뒤에도 계속 이어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The organization has continued even after its founder passed away.

examples.ko: 우리는 창립자께 감사하는 마음으로 행사를 열었어요.
examples.en: We held the event in gratitude to the founder.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '설립자', '창업자'가 있어요. 회사를 직접 시작한 사람은 '창업자', 학교나 재단은 '설립자'라고 하는 경우가 많고, '창립자'는 단체와 회사 모두에 써요. 존경하는 뜻으로 '창립자님'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: Close words are '설립자' and '창업자'. The person who started a business is often a '창업자', and schools or foundations tend to have a '설립자', while '창립자' works for both groups and companies. Out of respect you can say '창립자님'.

examples.en: Frozen meat needs to be thawed.

examples.ko: 해동 시간이 길어서 아침에 꺼내 놨어요.
examples.en: Thawing takes a long time, so I took it out in the morning.
I tried the microwave's defrost function.
Cook it right after it's thawed.

examples.ko: 급속 해동은 맛을 떨어뜨릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Quick thawing can make food taste worse.
I didn't know how to thaw it, so I searched online.

explain: 음식 이야기에서 가장 많이 써요. 자연의 얼음이 녹는 일은 보통 '해빙'이라고 해요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '자연 해동', '급속 해동', '해동 시간'이에요.
explain_en: It is used most in talk about food. Ice melting in nature is usually called '해빙'. Common partners are '자연 해동', '급속 해동', and '해동 시간'.

en: be unfrozen; be defrosted; be thawed

examples.en: The frozen shrimp haven't thawed yet.
Meat thaws quickly if you leave it at room temperature.
Frozen bread gets soft once it thaws.
Please wash the fish once it is fully thawed.

examples.ko: 전자레인지에서 밥이 해동되는 데 삼 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes three minutes for rice to defrost in the microwave.
I took it out in the morning and it was fully thawed by evening.

explain: '해동되다'는 음식이 녹아서 풀린 결과에 초점이 있어요. 하는 사람이 보일 때는 '해동하다'를 써요. '고기가 해동됐어요'와 '고기를 해동했어요'를 구별해 보세요.
explain_en: '해동되다' focuses on the result: food that has thawed. When a person does the thawing, use '해동하다'. Compare '고기가 해동됐어요' with '고기를 해동했어요'.

examples.en: I thawed the frozen meat last night.
I thawed the shrimp and put it in the fried rice.

examples.ko: 냉동 만두는 해동하지 말고 바로 쪄요.
examples.en: Don't thaw frozen dumplings; steam them right away.
I know how to defrost bread in the microwave.

examples.ko: 국물은 천천히 해동해야 맛이 덜 변해요.
examples.en: If you thaw broth slowly, the taste changes less.
I put the frozen rice on a plate to thaw it.

explain: '~을 해동하다'로 쓰고 대상은 보통 냉동식품이에요. '고기를 해동하다', '밥을 해동하다'처럼요. 구어체로는 '녹이다'도 써서 '냉동 만두를 녹여요'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It takes an object, usually frozen food: '고기를 해동하다', '밥을 해동하다'. In casual speech '녹이다' also works, as in '냉동 만두를 녹여요'.

examples.en: At today's concert they'll play a piano concerto.
That violinist played a Beethoven concerto.
A concerto is played by a soloist and an orchestra together.
I study while listening to a Mozart concerto.

examples.ko: 이 협주곡의 마지막 악장이 제일 빨라요.
examples.en: The last movement of this concerto is the fastest.
I like symphonies more than concertos.

explain: '피아노 협주곡', '바이올린 협주곡'처럼 악기 이름이 앞에 와요. 혼자 연주하는 '독주곡'이나 여러 악기가 함께하는 '교향곡'과 달라요. 한국어로는 '콘체르토'보다 '협주곡'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The instrument name comes first, as in '피아노 협주곡' and '바이올린 협주곡'. It differs from a solo piece, '독주곡', and from a symphony, '교향곡'. In Korean people say '협주곡' rather than '콘체르토'.

examples.ko: 안개 속에서 사람 같은 형체를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a human-like figure in the fog.

examples.ko: 불에 타서 가구의 형체도 알아볼 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The furniture burned so badly its shape was unrecognizable.

examples.ko: 어둠 속에서 아무 형체도 보이지 않았어요.
examples.en: I could not see any shape in the dark.
The snowman melted and only a rough shape was left.
The outline of a big animal moved in the distance.
The child was startled by a blurry shape.

explain: '형체가 없다', '형체를 알아볼 수 없다', '형체가 보이다'처럼 부정이나 흐릿한 상태와 자주 써요. '모양'은 눈에 보이는 일반적인 생김새이고, 형체는 물체로서의 윤곽에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 '예쁜 형체'보다 '예쁜 모양'이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It often appears with negatives or blurry things: '형체가 없다', '형체를 알아볼 수 없다', '형체가 보이다'. '모양' is general appearance, while 형체 focuses on a thing's outline as an object. So '예쁜 모양' sounds more natural than '예쁜 형체'.

examples.en: Items from the Korean Empire's imperial family are in the museum.
News about Japan's imperial family was in the newspaper.

examples.ko: 황실의 결혼식은 전 세계에서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The imperial wedding became a topic of talk worldwide.
Members of the imperial family visited the palace.
This porcelain was used by the imperial family.
There is a program where you can try imperial cuisine.

explain: 황제가 있는 나라의 왕가는 '황실', 왕이 있는 나라는 '왕실'이라고 구별해요. 한국사에서는 조선 때까지 '왕실', 대한제국 때(1897~1910)는 '황실'이라고 해요. 영국은 왕이 있어서 '영국 왕실'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A family with an emperor is a '황실', and one with a king is a '왕실'. In Korean history it is '왕실' through the Joseon period and '황실' during the Korean Empire (1897-1910). Britain has a king or queen, so it is '영국 왕실'.

en: in a rush of heat; hotly; burningly

examples.ko: 방에 들어가자 후끈 더운 공기가 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: When I entered the room, I felt a wave of hot air.
I was embarrassed and my face flushed hot.
I turned on the heater and the room warmed up quickly.

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 먹었더니 온몸이 후끈 더워졌어요.
examples.en: After eating spicy food, my whole body got hot.

examples.ko: 열차 문이 열리자 후끈 열기가 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: When the train door opened, a rush of heat came in.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears burned.

explain: '후끈 달아오르다', '후끈 더워지다'처럼 갑자기 열기가 확 느껴질 때 써요. 부끄러움이나 화로 얼굴이 뜨거워질 때도 쓰고, 분위기가 뜨거울 때 '분위기가 후끈 달아오르다'라고도 해요. 약하게 따뜻한 건 '따끈'이 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when heat suddenly hits you, as in '후끈 달아오르다' and '후끈 더워지다'. It also fits a face heating up from embarrassment or anger, and a heated mood, '분위기가 후끈 달아오르다'. For gentle warmth, '따끈' fits better.

examples.en: It's stifling hot inside the bus in midsummer.
I lit the stove and the room got toasty hot.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 후끈한 걸 보니 열이 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My face feels hot, so I think I have a fever.

examples.ko: 후끈하게 데운 국물을 마시니 몸이 풀려요.
examples.en: Drinking the piping hot broth relaxes my body.

examples.ko: 경기장 분위기가 후끈해서 모두 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: The stadium atmosphere was fired up, so everyone cheered loudly.

examples.ko: 오븐 문을 열자 후끈한 바람이 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the oven door, a blast of hot air came out.

explain: 공기나 몸이 덥고 열이 확 오르는 느낌에 써요. '따뜻하다'보다 열기가 세고 '뜨겁다'보다는 부드러워요. 사람의 열정이나 분위기가 뜨거울 때도 '분위기가 후끈하다'라고 써요.
explain_en: It describes air or a body that feels hot with heat rising suddenly. It is stronger than '따뜻하다' but gentler than '뜨겁다'. A passionate mood can also be '분위기가 후끈하다'.

examples.en: The revised edition of the dictionary came out this month.
Many new words were added in the revised edition.
The teacher told us to use the revised textbook.
The revised edition and the first edition have different page counts.

examples.ko: 저자가 십 년 만에 개정판을 냈어요.
examples.en: The author put out a revised edition after ten years.

examples.ko: 이 책은 두 번째 개정판이라서 내용이 더 정확해요.
examples.en: This is the second revised edition, so the content is more accurate.

explain: 책의 판은 '초판', '개정판', '증보판'처럼 불러요. 개정판은 틀린 곳을 고치거나 새 내용을 넣었을 때, 증보판은 내용을 늘렸을 때 많이 써요. 서점에서는 '개정판 출간'이라고 광고해요.
explain_en: Book editions are called things like '초판', '개정판', and '증보판'. A 개정판 corrects mistakes or adds new content, while a 증보판 expands it. Bookstores advertise a new one as '개정판 출간'.

examples.en: A small stream runs through the middle of the city.
Children are splashing in the stream.
When it rains, the stream swells.
I walked along the path beside the stream.

examples.ko: 개천 물이 맑아서 작은 물고기가 보여요.
examples.en: The stream water is clear, so I can see small fish.
Cherry blossoms bloomed along the stream.

explain: '강'보다 작고 '시내', '냇물'과 비슷한 곳을 가리켜요. 도시에서는 '청계천'처럼 '천'이 붙은 이름이 많고, 말할 때는 '개천'이 가장 쉬운 말이에요.

phrases.example: 가난한 집 아이가 의사가 되다니, 개천에서 용 났네요.
phrases.en: A dragon rises from the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 환경에서 훌륭한 사람이 나왔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when someone from a humble background becomes very successful.

explain_en: It is smaller than a '강' and close to '시내' and '냇물'. In cities many streams have names ending in '천', like '청계천', but in speech '개천' is the easiest word.

examples.en: My older brother majors in architecture at university.
In architecture class, we built a model house.
The architecture professor explained the structure of a hanok.

examples.ko: 건축학 책을 읽으면 건물이 달리 보여요.
examples.en: After reading an architecture book, buildings look different.
After graduating from the architecture department, I joined a design office.
That building is very special from an architectural point of view.

explain: 학문 이름이라서 '건축학과'(학과), '건축학자'(사람)로 많이 써요. 집을 짓는 일 자체는 '건축'이나 '건설'이라고 하고, '건축가'는 건물을 설계하는 사람이에요. 전공을 말할 때는 '건축'이라고 줄여 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: As a field of study it appears as '건축학과' (department) and '건축학자' (scholar). Building itself is '건축' or '건설', and a '건축가' designs buildings. When naming a major, people often shorten it to '건축'.

examples.en: Pulling an all-nighter the day before an exam is a no-no.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 짠 음식은 금물이라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said salty food is off limits.

examples.ko: 다이어트 중에 굶는 건 금물인데 자꾸 굶게 돼요.
examples.en: Starving yourself on a diet is a no-no, but I keep doing it.

examples.ko: 산에서는 불 피우는 게 금물이니까 조심하세요.
examples.en: Making a fire in the mountains is forbidden, so be careful.
Overpacked schedules were a no-no on the trip.
Impatience is counted as something to avoid when studying.

explain: '~은/는 금물이다' 틀로 쓰고, 하지 말아야 할 행동이나 습관을 조언하는 말투예요. 법으로 막는 '금지'와 달리 안 하는 게 좋다는 경고에 가까워요. 앞에는 주로 행동을 나타내는 명사가 와요.
explain_en: It is used in the pattern '~은/는 금물이다' to advise against an action or habit. Unlike '금지', which is a ban, it is closer to a warning that you'd better not. The word before it is mostly an action noun.

en: foot of a mountain; slope; shore edge

examples.ko: 산 밑 기슭에 작은 절이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small temple at the foot of the mountain.

examples.ko: 눈이 녹아서 언덕 기슭에 꽃이 피었어요.
examples.en: The snow melted and flowers bloomed at the foot of the hill.

examples.ko: 마을은 한라산 기슭을 따라 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: The village stretches long along the foot of Hallasan.

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 저쪽 기슭이 붉게 물들어요.
examples.en: When the sun sets, the foot of the slope over there turns red.
Reeds are growing along the lake's edge.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 기슭 마을이 위험해졌어요.
examples.en: With so much rain, the village at the slope's foot became dangerous.

explain: '산기슭'처럼 산이나 언덕이 끝나는 아래쪽 부분에 써요. 위쪽은 '산꼭대기'나 '정상', 가운데는 '산허리'예요. 강이나 바다의 가장자리는 '기슭'보다 '강가', '바닷가'가 더 일상적이에요.
explain_en: It is used like '산기슭' for the lower part where a mountain or hill ends. The top is '산꼭대기' or '정상', and the middle is '산허리'. For river or sea edges, '강가' and '바닷가' are more everyday than '기슭'.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한국어 공부의 좋은 길잡이가 돼요.
examples.en: This book is a good guide for studying Korean.
Stars were the guide for sailors in the old days.
The map served as a guide for the trip.

examples.ko: 선생님은 제게 인생의 길잡이 같은 분이에요.
examples.en: My teacher is like a guiding light in my life.
Using the signs as a guide, I walked along the forest path.
I made a guide video for beginners.

explain: 책 제목에 '~ 길잡이'가 많아서 '입문서'처럼 쓰여요. 길을 안내하는 사람은 '안내자'나 '가이드'라고 해요. 비유로 '인생의 길잡이'라고 하면 좋은 선생님이나 조언을 가리켜요.
explain_en: Book titles often end in '~ 길잡이', where it works like '입문서' (an intro guide). A person who leads the way is a '안내자' or '가이드'. As a metaphor, '인생의 길잡이' means a good teacher or piece of advice.

examples.en: I put an orchid pot in the living room.

examples.ko: 난초는 물을 너무 많이 주면 죽어요.
examples.en: An orchid dies if you give it too much water.
The orchid bloomed white and smells lovely.
I gave the teacher an orchid as a gift.
Orchid paintings often appear in East Asian painting.

examples.ko: 이 난초는 일 년에 한 번 꽃이 피어요.
examples.en: This orchid blooms once a year.

explain: 개업이나 승진 축하 선물로 '난 화분'을 많이 보내요. 줄여서 '난'이라고도 해요. 옛 그림에서는 매화·난초·국화·대나무, 즉 '사군자'의 하나예요.
explain_en: Orchid pots are a popular gift for a business opening or a promotion. It is shortened to '난'. In old paintings it is one of the '사군자': plum, orchid, chrysanthemum, and bamboo.

examples.en: I opened a cafe with a friend as partners.

examples.ko: 동업은 처음에 계약서를 잘 써야 해요.
examples.en: In a partnership, you need a good contract from the start.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 동업이 오 년 만에 끝났어요.
examples.en: The two people's partnership ended after five years.

examples.ko: 동업 상대를 고를 때는 신뢰가 제일 중요해요.
examples.en: When choosing a business partner, trust matters most.
Doing business with family can easily lead to fights.

examples.ko: 우리는 그 동업 제안을 정중히 거절했어요.
examples.en: We politely turned down that partnership offer.

explain: '동업을 하다/시작하다/정리하다'처럼 써요. 직장에서 같이 일하는 '동료'와 달라서, 돈과 책임을 나눠서 같이 사업하는 사이를 말해요. '친구와는 동업하지 마라'는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It goes with '동업을 하다', '시작하다', and '정리하다'. It differs from a coworker, '동료': partners share money and responsibility in a business. You often hear the saying '친구와는 동업하지 마라'.

examples.ko: 저는 대학 친구와 작은 가게를 동업해요.
examples.en: I run a small shop in partnership with a college friend.
We were business partners for three years.
Business partners share the profits.

examples.ko: 동업하기 전에 역할을 먼저 나눠 두세요.
examples.en: Divide the roles before you go into business together.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 새 사업을 동업할 거예요.
examples.en: The two companies will run the new business jointly.
We split the money we earned together fifty-fifty.

explain: '~와/과 동업하다'로 써요. 한 사람이 가게를 열고 다른 사람이 일만 돕는 건 동업이 아니라 '고용'이에요. 투자만 하는 사람은 '동업자'보다 '투자자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used as '~와/과 동업하다'. If one person owns the shop and the other just helps, that is '고용' (employment), not 동업. Someone who only invests is called a '투자자' rather than a '동업자'.
